title: Redirect rule item (erMatchRule)
$comment: The DynamoDB item shape the Lambda@Edge reads for a redirect (viewer-request). Modeled on EdgeRedirectRule/MatchCondition from the source project's redirect-rule-types.ts.

pk.description: Host, e.g. www.example.com. DynamoDB partition key.

sk.description: REDIRECT#<priority>, priority zero-padded to 5 digits; lower = higher priority; unique per host per type.

redirectURL.description: Where the rule sends the request: an absolute http(s) URL, or a root-relative path starting with "/" — and a path means a path on this host, so "//host" and "/\host" are not paths. This is the console's "Relative URL" toggle — one field, two forms.
redirectURL.$comment: Kept in step with the console's own check (ruleDraft.ts REDIRECT_TARGET), so a value the form accepts is never refused by the API — including the scheme's case, which is why it is spelled as character classes: draft-07 `pattern` has no case-insensitive flag. Two things it is deliberately strict about, both because the value is written to a Location header verbatim: whitespace anywhere, since a raw CR/LF would split the response; and a second "/" or a "\\" after the first slash, since the browser resolves "//evil.example.com" against the scheme alone and leaves the host entirely — a path that is not a path on this host. `$1` capture references are unaffected.

disabled.$comment: Optional; absent means enabled. The Lambda@Edge filters out rules where disabled=true (RulesService.loadRules), so a toggle takes effect within the edge cache TTL (~1 min). The console writes it through PATCH.

match.$comment: Shared match condition, referenced by rewrite-rule.schema.json. Field names/enums mirror MatchCondition + MatchType/MatchOperator in redirect-rule-types.ts.

headerName.description: Required when matchType is "header"; disallowed otherwise.
